Image caption, Labour MP Conor Rand says hotels are "not suitable" places to house asylum seekers In 2023, at the peak of the policy of housing asylum seekers in hotels, 400 were in use at a cost of £9m a day, according to the government. title: Demolition of Rochdale's Seven Sisters flats devastating, residents say

input.lead: Residents who have been informed that their flats will be bulldozed say they will continue to "fight"
input.summary: Residents who have been informed that their flats will be bulldozed say they will continue to "fight"
input.evidence_text: Demolition of Rochdale's Seven Sisters flats devastating, residents say - BBC News Image caption, Christina Hartley and Roy Kitcher say the flats are "home" and they do not want to move By Davinia Ramos , Reporting from in Rochdale and Rebecca Brahde , North West Published 1 hour ago Residents of a town's tower blocks which are set to be demolished have said it is "devastating" but they will continue to "fight" the decision. Rochdale's Seven Sisters tower blocks, which contain 766 flats, will be replaced by about 600 homes , social landlord Rochdale Boroughwide Housing (RBH) has said. Demolition of the tower blocks was first proposed in 2017 but was ruled out in 2023 after a local campaign against it, but residents began moving out in October 2025 over long-term safety concerns. Roy Kitcher and Christina Hartley, who have lived in one of the blocks for 14 years, said they were left "upset" and "angry". RBH said demolition was the only "realistic and affordable" option. Kitcher said: "It's devastating news - why they want to knock them down, I don't know." The couple are one of 78 households yet to accept an offer of another home. "This is home and I want to stay here, I don't want to be moving out again," Kitcher added. Hartley said: "I'm just so upset about it and angry." She said the council had asked her to look at accommodation, however it was not in the town. "I want to stay in Rochdale, I'm a Rochdale girl born and bred and I won't move until they find me somewhere round here," she said. Image source, Reuters Image caption, The seven sisters in Rochdale were built in the 1960s A local campaign, previously backed by Rochdale Council, had appealed for the buildings to be refurbished rather than demolished. title: LCD Soundsystem to headline Platt Fields Park gigs in 2027

input.lead: The Manchester park will host a series of 25,000-capacity concerts over two weekends next summer
input.summary: The Manchester park will host a series of 25,000-capacity concerts over two weekends next summer
input.evidence_text: Large outdoor concerts are due to return to Manchester's Platt Fields Park next summer, with LCD Soundsystem named as the first headliner The American rock band will perform at the park in Fallowfield on 30 July 2027, with Young Fathers, Cowboy Hunters and DJs Erol Alkan and Luka Una also on the bill Organisers said the concert would be part of a series of shows, each with a capacity of 25,000, taking place over two weekends in late July and early August The events, called PlattForm, are being organised by The Warehouse Project, SJM Concerts and Live Nation, with more artists due to be announced in the coming weeks Platt Fields Park previously hosted the Parklife music festival from 2010 to 2012, before it moved to Heaton Park in 2013 to accommodate growing crowds Other music festivals have since taken place at the park, including Flashback Festival in 2022 and 2023

title: The rare opportunity to examine centuries-old Coptic manuscripts

input.summary: Hundreds of people were able to encounter their heritage first-hand at a church in Stockport

input.summary: While repairs could take weeks to complete, the railway's popular Santa Specials will still operate
input.evidence_text: A historical train carriage has been vandalised at the East Lancashire Railway ahead of the start of its popular Christmas services On Saturday, staff in Bury discovered one of the doors had been smashed, another badly damaged and food and drink scattered inside the 1950s buffet car General manager Lee Kenny said repairs could take weeks, delaying other maintenance work by the railway's team of staff and volunteers Kenny said the Santa Special steam trains - from Bury to Rawtenstall in Lancashire and back - would still run as planned on selected dates from 28 November until 24 December Food and drink, including crisps and cans of cider, had been taken out of boxes and strewn across the carriage. The situation has now left the council with a toxic problem to deal with Town hall bosses are set to carry out ‘urgent’ works at Royton Library due to the need to tackle toxic asbestos. Asbestos is a fibrous mineral that was valued for its strength and fireproofing capabilities in old buildings and was widely used It is now banned from use, but if disturbed where it is still present, those fibres cause severe, incurable lung diseases. Around 5,000 people are estimated to die from asbestos-related issues every year The library was refurbished as part of a major £4m scheme which finished in 2024. However, earlier this year, the library had to shut suddenly and has remained closed since A council report said that in July 2026, library staff ‘reported that flooring in certain areas was becoming ‘bouncy’’ and ‘severe signs of dry rot’ were later discovered. Further investigations were carried out once the library closed

That’s because only around 80 households remain from the original 766 since the original demolition announcement 10 years ago The uncertainty about the blocks' future has led many tenants to move on. The situation has now left the council with a toxic problem to deal with Town hall bosses are set to carry out ‘urgent’ works at Royton Library due to the need to tackle toxic asbestos. Asbestos is a fibrous mineral that was valued for its strength and fireproofing capabilities in old buildings and was widely used It is now banned from use, but if disturbed where it is still present, those fibres cause severe, incurable lung diseases. Around 5,000 people are estimated to die from asbestos-related issues every year The library was refurbished as part of a major £4m scheme which finished in 2024. However, earlier this year, the library had to shut suddenly and has remained closed since A council report said that in July 2026, library staff ‘reported that flooring in certain areas was becoming ‘bouncy’’ and ‘severe signs of dry rot’ were later discovered. input.evidence_text: The government's new Digital and Technologies Jobs Plan aims to create 200,000 entry-level jobs over the next decade, recognising the barriers facing employers and the importance of regional organisations in connecting people with opportunities. The government has published its D The plan acknowledges that the challenge is not simply a shortage of people with digital skills. Entry-level recruitment has become more difficult, with employers increasingly favouring experienced candidates and many graduates and other new entrants struggling to secure their fi Manchester Digital contributed to the development of the plan through its involvement in the government's Digital Skills Council, drawing on its work with employers and education providers across Greater Manchester Around 800,000 digital and technology roles are projected to need filling over the next decade. The plan sets out an ambition to create 200,000 entry-level jobs, including apprenticeships, during that period The plan also addresses how AI is changing workforce requirements and the importance of ensuring people entering the industry have both technical knowledge and practical workplace skills Manchester Digital's 2026 Sector Insights Report highlighted a reduction of around 20% in early-career opportunities, despite continued demand for experienced technology professionals
